Photograph: Prakash Mathema/AFP/Getty Images Nepal-Tibet flood disaster Search on for at least 33 Britons missing after flash floods in Nepal and Tibet Rescue teams trying to locate nearly 1,400 missing people, mostly tourists, after floods killed at least 353 Nepal-Tibet flash flood – latest updates Rachel Hall Thu 27 Aug 2026 10.24 EDT First published on Thu 27 Aug 2026 05.48 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Rescue teams in Nepal are searching for at least 33 British nationals who are among those missing after flash floods ravaged its border with Tibet , killing at least 353 people. Nearly 1,400 people are missing, most of them tourists, authorities have said, after a glacier collapse triggered floods that roared down valleys and razed entire villages . The tour company Kailash Journeys confirmed it had not been able to account for seven UK nationals – five women and two men aged between 18 and 55 – travelling with it. Another tour operator, the Trekkers’ Society, said among the British citizens who had been completing one of its tours to the sacred Hindu site of Mount Kailash were four males aged 14, 50, 50 and 54 and five women aged 40, 46, 50, 50 and 53. 9:21 ‘Tsunami from the sky:’ floods leave trail of devastation in Nepal and Tibet - The Latest Nearly 1,400 missing, mostly tourists, after Nepal-Tibet flash flood kills at least 270 Read more The tour operator Alpine Eco Trek said a 13-year-old girl was among the missing British nationals and two Irish citizens were also missing. They were on a nine-day tour to Mount Kailash and crossing into Tibet from Nepal when they became trapped at the border as the flash floods struck. Other missing British nationals with Alpine Eco Trek are three men aged 65, 64 and 52 and seven women aged 44, 47, 51, 60, 63, 63 and 65, according to travel logs. The tour company Himalayan Glacier US told the BBC it had lost contact with a group of 47 guests, including two British citizens, who were en route to Mount Kailash. Fishtail Tours, a Nepali travel agency, said one British person was missing. View image in fullscreen A damaged bridge in Galchhi, Nepal. Photograph: Francis Mascarenhas/Reuters Andy Burnham has pledged an initial £5m in UK government support and offered to send emergency responders and rescue support to assist Nepal’s disaster response efforts. Speaking to journalists during a visit to south Wales, he said: “It’s a devastating picture that is emerging from what has happened in Nepal. Scenes that we’ve never seen the like before, I don’t think, certainly the scale of the devastation. “So there is immediate action being taken. We are deploying consular support staff to the region so that British nationals will be able to access support 24/7. Obviously there are a number of British nationals who currently are thought to be missing and we’ll be providing all the support we can to their families in what is a very distressing and devastating situation.” In a statement, he added: “In the past, Nepal has been there for Britain in our hour of need, and we will be there for Nepal in its hour of need right now.” The president of the Nepal Centre for Disaster Management, Bishal Nath Upreti, told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme that the flash floods were like a “tsunami from the sky”. He said: “It’s a huge debris, and in fact, after the 2015 earthquake, this is one of the largest disasters that we have [had] in Nepal.” He added: “It was such a huge amount of water. You can imagine it is 20m cubic metres excess water on the river … Villages and villages along the almost 40 to 50 kilometres were completely wiped out.” location map The Nepal tourism board said on Wednesday that 33 UK citizens were among the foreign nationals unaccounted for. At least three people had died in Tibet, according to China’s state broadcaster CCTV, while the Xinhua news agency said 558 people were unaccounted for in the region. Rescuers are racing to locate people missing in the mountainous Rasuwa region, which borders China’s autonomous region of Tibet and is popular with trekkers and pilgrims. Pramod Poudel, from Uckfield, East Sussex, told the BBC that his wife, parents, brother and uncle had been caught in flash flooding. He said he would fly to Nepal on Thursday night to try to make contact with them. Poudel said: “I guess there is no power so they can’t charge their phones – to be honest, it’s a very hard and difficult time at the moment.” In an emotional interview, he said: “I have seen pictures of where my home town used to be … and there is nothing there now.” The UK government minister Pat McFadden told Times Radio the picture was “not completely clear yet”, with “many, many more” people understood to be missing than those reported by the Nepalese authorities, and no clear figures from China yet. Mudslide submerges China-Nepal crossing point – video He said: “In terms of missing Britons, my colleague the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, has posted on social media phone numbers that people can call for further information. “But it’s a fast-moving picture. We don’t have a full picture yet of the numbers missing.” The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office said it was “deeply saddened by the loss of life and devastation caused by the floods in Nepal”. It added: “British nationals in Nepal should follow local authority advice and exercise caution while travelling. Beállítom Szoboszlai Dominik három éve igazolt a Liverpoolhoz, ez idő alatt pedig nem pusztán helytállt, hanem sokszor ő volt a csapat húzóembere. Szoboszlai bajnoki címet is ünnepelhetett már Liverpoolban, és hol bombagólokkal , hol azzal tűnt ki, hogy minden poszton felszántotta a pályát, ahova berakták. A szurkolók az előző idényben ötször választották őt a hónap játékosának , nyáron hosszabbított is a csapatnál , így láthatóan mindenki elégedett vele Liverpoolban. Annyira, hogy a 99. helyen ő is bekerült a Liverpool friss kiadványába, amelyben szurkolók, volt játékosok, újságírók és a klub saját zsűrije szavazták meg a klub történetének 100 legjobb játékosát. Az ide kattintva elérhető lista eleje aligha okoz meglepetést bárkinek, aki követi az angol focit, az első öt helyre olyan klublegendák kerültek, mint Steven Gerrard, Kenny Dalglish, Ian Rush, Mohamed Szaláh és John Barnes. Innentől aztán már egyre többet lehet vitatkozni azon, hogy megérdemelten vannak-e ott bizonyos játékosok, ahol, amit már jóval a kiadvány megjelenése előtt meg is tettek a szurkolók az interneten, miután a Liverpool az elmúlt hónapokban szép lassan az egész listát közzétette. De ez persze nem változtat azon, hogy a most megjelent könyvben ez lett a sorrend. Ez pedig azt jelenti, hogy Szoboszlai három év alatt úgy belopta magát a liverpooliak szívébe, hogy már most a klub történetének 99. legjobb játékosaként tartják számon. Ide kattintva azt is el lehet olvasni, hogy miért: röviden azért, mert a távoli lövései halálosak, és egy igazi igásló a pályán. Meg persze azért is, mert hatalmas gólokat tud lőni, két szabadrúgásból szerzett találatot külön ki is emeltek. Az egyik az, amit az Arsenalnak lőtt , amit tavaly a szezon góljának választottak , a másik pedig az, amit a Manchester Citynek lőtt még februárban . A játékosok ugyan eddig is tudták, hogy benne lesznek a könyvben, hiszen a tartalmának nagy része már elérhető volt online, de most végre a kezükbe is foghatták a múlt héten megjelent kiadványt, többek közt Szoboszlai is megnézhette magát benne. Mint mondta, nagyszerű érzés, hogy benne lehet ebben a könyvben, aztán hozzátette, hogy amúgy megelőzte Alexis MacAllistert, aki a 100. helyre került. https://hungarytoday.hu/i-am-not-afraid-.text: “I am not afraid!” – FIDESZ Politician Writes from Prison Balázs Bús, the former FIDESZ mayor of Óbuda (Budapest’s 3rd District) and former vice president of the National Cultural Fund (NAK), has been held at Szeged’s Csillag Prison for four months. He has now addressed the public in an open letter. He describes the criminal proceedings against him as politically motivated and accuses Prime Minister Magyar of influencing the judiciary. The politician claims that authorities are trying to force him to make a false statement, but says he is unwilling to do so. He wrote the letter after a court extended his pretrial detention through Christmas. “I am not afraid!” These are the opening words of Balázs Bús’s letter, written on October 22 at Szeged’s maximum-security prison. The former mayor sharply criticizes the prosecution, the court, and Prime Minister Magyar, comparing his own imprisonment to the political reprisals that followed the suppression of the 1956 Revolution. According to Bús, he has been “wrongfully and unlawfully” detained for four months. He claims that the prosecution is under political pressure and expects him to confess to something that would contradict both the truth and his conscience. ❗️EVERYONE NEEDS TO READ THIS! This is Hungary today! An attempt to extract incriminating testimony through arbitrary detention and mistreatment. Just like the political show trials of the 1950s… Below is a message written from prison by Balázs Bús, a political prisoner, former Fidesz mayor of Budapest’s 3rd district, and former Vice President of Hungary’s National Cultural Fund. “I am not afraid! For four months now, I have been wrongfully and unlawfully held in Szeged’s Csillag Prison by the Bács-Kiskun County Prosecutor’s Office, which has been intimidated (abused) and placed under the direct control of Péter Magyar. Although I have fully cooperated with the prosecution and answered every question, the political masterminds behind this show-trial-style prosecution want me to give testimony that contradicts not only the truth and reality, but also my faith. Non possum! To achieve this, they have continuously restricted my ability to communicate with the outside world since the very beginning of the proceedings, seeking to sever and destroy my relationships with my family and loved ones. I am grateful to everyone who stands by them during these evil times and supports us through their prayers. I am especially grateful for the solidarity of our Polish friends! There are no legitimate grounds for my detention. There is no risk of flight, as my lawyer and I informed the investigative authorities even before my arrest that I was at their disposal. The alleged risk of reoffending is equally false and ridiculous, as is the claim that I might interfere with the proceedings. The prosecutor handling my case knows this perfectly well. The investigating judge at the Kecskemét District Court performs no meaningful judicial scrutiny, since it is common knowledge that judges in Kecskemét approve 100% of prosecutors’ requests (which, of course, raises the question of why these judges are needed at all). What is even more disturbing is that this has created an unchecked concentration of power in the hands of prosecutors, enabling abuses of authority, as my own case clearly demonstrates. But, to quote the words of András Visky: “Does it even make sense to question legality in an age when lawlessness itself has been enshrined in law?” In his speeches in Parliament and in Kisvárda, Péter Magyar made it absolutely clear to the authorities what verdict he expects them to deliver. It is beyond any doubt that I am the victim of a politically orchestrated show trial. In 1956, my father was 22 years old. As a soldier stationed in Esztergom, he stood on the side of the revolution. He never joined the Communist Party. In 1956, my mother was 20 years old. She survived the volley of gunfire unleashed by the ÁVO communist state security forces in Kossuth Square. She never joined the Communist Party. In 1988, at the age of 22, I joined Fidesz to help put an end to the one-party system, the tyranny that restricted our freedoms, and the communist party-state that had devastated my parents’ generation. In 1986, forty years ago, the political officer at the Cegléd military barracks and military counterintelligence tried to force me into giving false testimony. They failed. And now, in 2026, at the age of 60, I have become a political prisoner of resurgent Bolshevik hatred and power. After 1956, the ideological predecessors of Péter Magyar executed the martyr József Kováts here, in Szeged’s Csillag Prison. Within these very walls, I pray for him and for all the revolutionaries who were sentenced and imprisoned in Csillag as part of the reprisals following the 1956 Hungarian Revolution and War of Independence. Blessed be their memory. “We are hard pressed on every side, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair; persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed.” (2 Corinthians 4:8–9) “I give thanks for everything, even for being taken away, because through it I have drawn closer to God.” (János Esterházy) Csillag Prison, October 22, 2026 Memorial of Saint Pope John Paul II Balázs Bús I am not afraid!” — Balázs Orbán (@BalazsOrban_HU) October 24, 2026 “Although I have fully cooperated with the prosecution and answered every question, the political masterminds behind this show-trial-style prosecution want me to give testimony that contradicts not only the truth and reality, but also my faith. Non possum! ( ed.’s note – Latin: ‘I cannot do it’),” he declared. In his letter, the politician also claims that his contact with family members and relatives has been restricted since the proceedings began, which he views as part of the pressure being exerted on him. The publication of the letter is particularly significant because, on October 22, the Kecskemét District Court extended the politician’s pretrial detention by another two months, until December 25. According to a report on the court’s decision, the Bács-Kiskun County Chief Prosecutor’s Office had requested on October 19 that the detention order remain in effect. The investigating judge found that the reasonable suspicion of a crime and several specific grounds for detention continued to exist. The decision is not yet final. Bús, however, believes that neither the risk of flight nor the risk of reoffending justifies his continued detention. He points out that, before his arrest, he and his lawyer had already informed the authorities that he was willing to cooperate with the investigation. He also strongly criticizes judicial oversight. He claims that judges in Kecskemét approve every request submitted by the prosecution, which, in his view, has given prosecutors unchecked power. Bús had previously requested his release and the use of less restrictive measures, but his application was denied. In early October, his defense attorney, Gábor Papp, reported that the politician had given a detailed statement and answered all the prosecution’s questions. Bús was accused of breach of trust causing particularly substantial financial damage in connection with the use of funding from the National Cultural Fund (NKA). The investigation has since expanded to include several former senior government officials. Among those implicated in the case is former Minister of Culture and Innovation Balázs Hankó, who was placed in pretrial detention at the end of September. The handling of politically sensitive cases outside of the capital has raised questions about the choice of venue. Continue reading The former minister also described the proceedings as politically motivated and claimed that those involved were being detained without justification. In his latest letter, Bús essentially expresses the same position, but in much more personal and forceful terms than before. In addition to the NKA affair, the former mayor has also come under suspicion in the Óbuda corruption case. According to the prosecution, he allegedly accepted bribes while serving as mayor. Bús denies committing the alleged crimes. One of the most serious allegations in his letter is directed at Prime Minister Magyar himself: In his speeches in Parliament and in Kisvárda, Péter Magyar made it absolutely clear to the authorities what verdict he expects them to deliver. It is beyond any doubt that I am the victim of a politically orchestrated show trial,” he wrote. In the second half of the letter, Bús reflects on his family history and his own political past. He writes that his father, then a 22-year-old soldier, sided with the revolutionaries in 1956, while his mother survived the massacre in Kossuth Square at the age of 20. He emphasizes that neither of his parents ever joined the Communist Party. Regarding his own life, Bús writes that he joined FIDESZ in 1988, at the age of 22, to help abolish the one-party system and put an end to arbitrary rule. He also recalls that, according to his account, an attempt was made to force him into making a false confession during his military service in 1986, but he refused to give in to the pressure even then. “And now, in 2026, at the age of 60, I have become a political prisoner of resurgent Bolshevik hatred and power,” he writes. The Csillag Prison in Szeged. Photo: Public domain/Wikimedia Commons He also discusses the historical significance of Csillag Prison, paying tribute to József Kováts, who was executed following the 1956 Revolution, as well as to the revolutionaries imprisoned during the subsequent reprisals. Bús emphasizes that he continues to hold on to his Christian faith despite his imprisonment. He uses a biblical quotation and reflects on the writings of János Esterházy to convey that he sees his time in prison as both a spiritual trial and an opportunity to strengthen his faith. In his letter, the politician thanks everyone who has supported him and his family, singling out the solidarity shown by his Polish friends. Despite years of foreign-funded media campaign, prosecutors seem to have very little evidence to go by.
